hooks.prompt:
A git push just completed. Your job is to update progress_log.md in /home/user/claude_financetracker_pk91 to reflect what was just pushed.

Do the following steps in order:

1. Run: git -C /home/user/claude_financetracker_pk91 log --oneline -10
2. Run: git -C /home/user/claude_financetracker_pk91 diff HEAD~3 HEAD --stat 2>/dev/null || git -C /home/user/claude_financetracker_pk91 diff HEAD --stat
3. Read /home/user/claude_financetracker_pk91/progress_log.md
4. If the most recent commit message contains 'Auto-update progress_log', examine the commit before it — the log is being updated for the push BEFORE that auto-commit.
5. Add a new session entry (or extend today's entry if one already exists for today) that includes:
   - Date and version (infer version from existing log entries or commit messages)
   - A short 'What was pushed' summary based on commit messages
   - List of files changed and what each change does
   - Updated 'Last Updated:' date at the very top of the file
   - Updated footer line at the very bottom of the file
6. Write the updated file back to /home/user/claude_financetracker_pk91/progress_log.md
7. Run: git -C /home/user/claude_financetracker_pk91 add progress_log.md && git -C /home/user/claude_financetracker_pk91 commit -m 'Auto-update progress_log.md'
   IMPORTANT: Do NOT run git push — commit locally only. This prevents an infinite loop.

Match the existing style and section format already used in the file. Keep the new entry concise.
